candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16: monitor/evaluate client response to medication therapy and identify adverse effects
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — trastuzumab cardiotoxicity monitoring
candidate.educational_objective: Apply the labeled trastuzumab cardiac-monitoring schedule: obtain baseline LVEF and reassess every 3 months during therapy and upon completion because of cardiomyopathy risk.

options.A: Measure LVEF at baseline and every 3 months during treatment and upon completion
options.B: Check LVEF only if symptoms of heart failure develop
options.C: Measure LVEF once after treatment ends, with no baseline assessment
options.D: Replace LVEF monitoring with routine complete blood counts

candidate.rationale: HERCEPTIN can cause cardiomyopathy with decreased left ventricular ejection fraction. Current labeling recommends a thorough cardiac assessment, including LVEF determination by echocardiogram or MUGA scan, with a baseline LVEF immediately before treatment and LVEF measurements every 3 months during and upon completion of HERCEPTIN. Symptom-triggered monitoring alone is insufficient, and a complete blood count does not assess this toxicity. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Trastuzumab can cause cardiomyopathy/decreased LVEF and its current label recommends baseline LVEF plus measurements every 3 months during treatment and upon completion.
candidate.source_locator: Boxed Warning/§5.1 Cardiomyopathy — Cardiac Monitoring: conduct cardiac assessment including LVEF by echocardiogram or MUGA; baseline LVEF immediately prior to initiation; LVEF every 3 months during and upon completion of HERCEPTIN
candidate.source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
candidate.stem: A client is beginning intravenous trastuzumab (HERCEPTIN). Which cardiac-monitoring plan is consistent with the current prescribing information?
